title: Stored (Persistent) Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Attacker-supplied script is stored by the application and later rendered to other users without proper output encoding. When a victim views the affected page, the script executes in their browser in the context of the application, enabling session theft, account takeover, or actions performed as the victim, including administrators.
businessImpact: High --- persistent XSS can lead to session hijacking, credential theft, and administrative account compromise affecting many users.
remediation:
- Context-aware output encoding for all user-controlled data rendered in pages.
- Validate and sanitize input; use a vetted HTML sanitizer for rich content.
- Implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP).
- Set HttpOnly and Secure flags on session cookies.
